reasons.int32-overflow: ST_AsEncodedPolyline keeps each delta in a C int and computes delta * 2 in that int. A delta of 2^30 units or more wraps around, for example any step over 107.374 degrees at precision 7. Google's algorithm has no such limit.
reasons.int32-conversion: ST_AsEncodedPolyline converts each rounded value or delta to a C int. Outside the int range that conversion is undefined behavior; this amd64 build produces INT_MIN, which then doubles to 0 and encodes as "?".
reasons.non-finite: ST_AsEncodedPolyline encodes NaN and infinite coordinates (they convert to INT_MIN, see int32-conversion) instead of rejecting them. polytini throws a PolylineError with code "coordinate".
reasons.negative-precision: Both functions silently replace a negative precision with 5. polytini throws a PolylineError with code "option".
reasons.precision-overflow: At a precision where 10^precision is infinite (309 and up), ST_AsEncodedPolyline multiplies to infinity or NaN and ST_LineFromEncodedPolyline divides to zero. polytini allows precision 0 to 15.
reasons.srid: ST_AsEncodedPolyline only accepts geometries with SRID 4326 and raises an error for any other SRID, including none.
reasons.geometry-type: ST_AsEncodedPolyline only accepts LINESTRING and MULTIPOINT, so a single POINT is an error, while Google's algorithm encodes a one point sequence.
reasons.high-bytes: ST_LineFromEncodedPolyline reads the UTF-8 bytes of the text and only rejects bytes below "?" (63). DEL (127) and every byte of a non-ASCII character count as continuation chunks, so such strings decode to coordinates. Google's alphabet is "?" to "~" and polytini rejects anything else (code "char").
reasons.repeated-points: ST_LineFromEncodedPolyline drops a point that is equal to the point before it (it appends with ptarray_append_point(..., LW_FALSE)), so "????" decodes to one point, not two. Google's algorithm returns every point, and so does polytini.
reasons.varint-32bit: ST_LineFromEncodedPolyline reads each value into 32 bits and raises "coordinate value is too large" for anything wider, including more than 6 zero padding chunks. Google's algorithm has no such limit; polytini decodes values exactly up to 2^53.
reasons.int32-range: ST_LineFromEncodedPolyline keeps the running sums in 32 bit ints and raises "coordinate value is too large" when one leaves that range, for example latitude 90 at precision 10. polytini has no such limit.
